   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# PULPO Optimization Framework: Complete Demonstration\n",
    "\n",
    "This notebook provides a comprehensive demonstration of PULPO's capabilities for sustainable technology optimization, covering basic single-objective optimization through advanced uncertainty analysis and multi-objective trade-off exploration."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "fc21234c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 1. System Description\n",
    "\n",
    "The demonstration system models interconnected background and foreground processes for low-carbon methanol production:\n",
    "\n",
    "**Background System** supplies conventional commodities:\n",
    "- Natural gas extraction and electricity generation\n",
    "- Wind electricity generation  \n",
    "- Water supply\n",
    "- Hydrogen production via steam methane reforming (SMR)\n",
    "- Oxygen production via air separation unit (ASU)\n",
    "\n",
    "**Foreground System** represents novel technologies:\n",
    "- Hydrogen electrolysis (producing H₂ and O₂ as byproduct)\n",
    "- Direct air capture (DAC) for CO₂ supply\n",
    "- Methanol synthesis using captured CO₂ and H₂\n",
    "- Ozone production consuming oxygen\n",
    "\n",
    "**Multifunctional Links**: The O₂-byproduct and O₂-market activities balance oxygen flows between electrolysis byproduct recovery and conventional supply, ensuring proper system allocation.\n",
    "\n",
    "**Environmental Flows**: The system tracks emissions of CO₂, CH₄, particulate matter (PM), and water use to the biosphere.\n",
    "\n",
    "This represents an integrated Power-to-Methanol pathway with linked energy and material exchanges between renewable and fossil-based subsystems.\n",
    "\n",
    "![Flowchart of the system](data/pulpo_showcase.png)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "76511589",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 1.1 Technology Choices and System Interdependencies\n",
    "\n",
    "The system incorporates several critical technological choices that determine environmental performance:\n",
    "\n",
    "**Energy Supply Alternatives:**\n",
    "- Electricity generation: Natural gas combined-cycle (NGCC) vs. wind power\n",
    "- Represents background system choices reflecting alternative energy mixes\n",
    "\n",
    "**Hydrogen Production Pathways:**\n",
    "- Steam methane reforming (SMR) in background system\n",
    "- Water electrolysis in foreground system  \n",
    "- Demonstrates foreground-background substitution dynamics\n",
    "\n",
    "**Oxygen Supply Options:**\n",
    "- Conventional production via air separation unit (ASU) in background\n",
    "- Recovery as electrolysis byproduct in foreground\n",
    "- Market-based supply balancing both sources\n",
    "\n",
    "The O₂-market activity ensures that multiple oxygen sources can coexist or compete depending on system boundaries and optimization objectives."
   ]
  },

   "id": "c90925a2",

     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "foreground_db created with 6 activities and uncertainty added to exchanges.\n",
      "Registered 3 LCIA methods.\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "from pulpo import pulpo\n",
    "pulpo.setup_sample_db()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f53b0cf5",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 2.2 Library Import\n",
    "\n",
    "Import required libraries for optimization analysis and data manipulation."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "c459cca2",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import sys\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import copy"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a882d243",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 2.3 PULPO Configuration\n",
    "\n",
    "Configure the PULPO optimizer with:\n",
    "- **Project name**: Identifier for optimization project\n",
    "- **Databases**: Background (conventional) and foreground (novel) systems\n",
    "- **Methods**: Impact assessment categories with relative weights\n",
    "  - Climate change: weight = 1 (primary objective)\n",
    "  - Resources: weight = 0 (inactive initially)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "a2f93f81",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from pulpo.utils.utils import is_bw25\n",
    "\n",
    "project = \"sample_project_bw25\" if is_bw25() else \"sample_project\"\n",
    "database = [\"background_db\", \"foreground_db\"]\n",
    "method = {\"('my project', 'climate change')\": 1,\n",
    "          \"('my project', 'resources')\": 0,}"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "01d89a3f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 2.4 Optimizer Initialization\n",
    "\n",
    "Create the PULPO optimizer instance."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "726f2139",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "pulpo_worker = pulpo.PulpoOptimizer(project, database, method)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f11a6898",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "> **⚠️ Attention:**  \n",
    "> PULPO assumes that the biosphere in your project is named **`biosphere3`**.  \n",
    "> If your project uses a different biosphere name, make sure to explicitly provide it to your PULPO worker.  \n",
    ">  \n",
    "> For example:\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "pulpo_worker.intervention_matrix = \"ecoinvent-3.10-biosphere\"\n",
    "```\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "bde304d9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 2.5 Life Cycle Inventory Data Loading\n",
    "\n",
    "Load technosphere matrix (A), biosphere matrix (B), and process/intervention mappings. This creates the mathematical foundation for optimization by establishing the linear system: **Ax = f** and **environmental impacts = Bx**."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "82d48799",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "pulpo_worker.get_lci_data()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "3fcb751c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 3. Single-Objective Optimization Examples\n",
    "\n",
    "### 3.1 Functional Unit Definition\n",
    "\n",
    "The functional unit defines the reference output for environmental impact assessment. We begin with 1 kg methanol as the primary product demand."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "2acfad63",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "methanol_process = pulpo_worker.retrieve_processes(reference_products='methanol')\n",
    "\n",
    "demand = {methanol_process[0]: 1}"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "17b70c81",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 3.2 Technology Choice Definition\n",
    "\n",
    "Define alternative technologies for key system components:\n",
    "\n",
    "**Electricity Generation:**\n",
    "- Wind electricity (renewable)\n",
    "- Natural gas electricity (fossil-based)\n",
    "\n",
    "**Hydrogen Production:**\n",
    "- Steam methane reforming (SMR) - conventional background process\n",
    "- Water electrolysis - novel foreground process\n",
    "\n",
    "**Oxygen Supply:**\n",
    "- Air separation unit (ASU) - conventional production\n",
    "- Market supply - generic oxygen source\n",
    "- Electrolysis byproduct - recovered from hydrogen production\n",
    "\n",
    "These alternatives represent the core technological decisions determining system environmental performance."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "41d95cfd",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "## Electricity Choice\n",
    "electricity_technologies = [\"wind electricity\",\n",
    "                            \"natural gas electricity\",]\n",
    "electricity_processes = pulpo_worker.retrieve_processes(processes=electricity_technologies)\n",
    "\n",
    "## Hydrogen Choice\n",
    "hydrogen_technologies = [\"hydrogen SMR\",\n",
    "                         \"hydrogen electrolysis\",]\n",
    "hydrogen_processes = pulpo_worker.retrieve_processes(processes=hydrogen_technologies)\n",
    "\n",
    "## Oxygen Choice\n",
    "oxygen_technologies = [\"O2-market\",\n",
    "                       \"O2 ASU\",]\n",
    "oxygen_processes = pulpo_worker.retrieve_processes(processes=oxygen_technologies)\n",
    "\n",
    "### Oxygen byproduct\n",
    "oxygen_aux = \"O2-byproduct\"\n",
    "oxygen_byproduct = pulpo_worker.retrieve_processes(processes=[oxygen_aux])\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "3ba9003f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 3.3 Choices Dictionary Configuration\n",
    "\n",
    "Organize technology alternatives into an optimization-ready structure. Each choice category contains multiple alternatives with capacity constraints.\n",
    "\n",
    "> **⚠️ Attention:**  \n",
    "> A capacity of `float('inf')` means *no limit*: the solver is not restricted by it.  \n",
    "> Give an alternative a finite capacity only where it has a real limit. A huge finite number such as `1e10` adds  \n",
    "> nothing and can degrade the solver's numerics; leave it infinite instead.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "8aafd1fa",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "## Choices\n",
    "choices = {\n",
    "    \"Electricity\": {electricity_processes[0]: float('inf'),\n",
    "                    electricity_processes[1]: float('inf')},\n",
    "    \"Hydrogen\": {hydrogen_processes[0]: float('inf'),\n",
    "                 hydrogen_processes[1]: float('inf')},\n",
    "    \"Oxygen\": {oxygen_processes[0]: float('inf'), \n",
    "               oxygen_processes[1]: float('inf'),},\n",
    "}"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "eb884274",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 3.4 Lower Bound Constraints\n",
    "\n",
    "Configure process flow constraints. The O₂-byproduct process requires non-negative flow (≥ 0) to ensure physically meaningful byproduct recovery from electrolysis."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 10,
   "id": "7561033e",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# Lower bound\n",
    "lower_bound = {oxygen_byproduct[0]: 0}"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "cd77d1a9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "> **⚠️ Attention:**  \n",
    "> With this configuration, the O₂ by-product is **allowed to be vented** (e.g., to a market or directly to the environment).\n",
    "> If you want to **force the system to internally utilize the by-product**, you must also specify an **upper bound of `0`**, which prevents any venting and requires full integration within the production system.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9eb88b82",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 3.5 First Optimization: Single Product\n",
    "\n",
    "Solve optimization with 1 kg methanol demand. PULPO identifies the technology combination minimizing climate change impact while satisfying demand constraints."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "ba7220d7",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Creating Instance\n",
      "Instance created\n",
      "optimal solution found:  1.7471600582975855\n",
      "Optimization problem solved using Highspy\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "pulpo_worker.instantiate(choices=choices, demand=demand, lower_limit=lower_bound)\n",
    "results = pulpo_worker.solve()"
   ]
  },

   "cell_type": "markdown",

   "source": [

    "\n",
    "These constraints force optimization within technological feasibility bounds."
   ]

   "source": [
    "### 4.3 Impact Category Switching\n",
    "\n",
    "Demonstrate objective function flexibility by switching from climate change to resource use optimization. Different environmental priorities lead to distinct technology choices."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 23,
   "id": "d6ef6773",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [

    "          \"('my project', 'resources')\": 1,}"
   ]
  },

   "id": "e5b972e0",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c9e1fa48",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 5. Summary: Core PULPO Capabilities\n",
    "\n",
    "This demonstration covered PULPO's fundamental optimization features:\n",
    "\n",
    "**System Integration:**\n",
    "- Multi-database integration (background + foreground systems)\n",
    "- Technology choice optimization across energy, hydrogen, and oxygen sources\n",
    "- Multi-product system optimization with material flow synergies\n",
    "\n",
    "**Constraint Handling:**\n",
    "- Technology capacity constraints (realistic deployment limits)\n",
    "- Resource availability constraints (scarcity scenarios)\n",
    "- Process flow constraints (physical feasibility)\n",
    "\n",
    "**Multi-Criteria Analysis:**\n",
    "- Objective function flexibility (climate change vs. resource use)\n",
    "- Technology trade-off analysis under different environmental priorities\n",
    "- Impact assessment across multiple environmental categories"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "aa9d9470",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 6. Multi-Objective Optimization: Pareto Front Analysis\n",
    "\n",
    "Explore trade-offs between competing objectives through Pareto front generation. This analysis reveals how environmental performance varies when balancing climate change and resource use priorities using the epsilon-constraint method."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "1d1787c8",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 6.1 Multi-Objective Setup\n",
    "\n",
    "Create dual-objective PULPO worker with equal weighting for both climate change and resource use objectives to establish baseline performance ranges."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 27,
   "id": "3af5a051",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Multi-objective PULPO worker created with both climate change and resource use objectives\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Create multi-objective method configuration\n",
    "methods_multi = {\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'climate change')\": 1,\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'resources')\": 1\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "# Initialize multi-objective PULPO worker\n",
    "pulpo_worker_multi = pulpo.PulpoOptimizer(project, database, methods_multi)\n",
    "pulpo_worker_multi.get_lci_data()\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"Multi-objective PULPO worker created with both climate change and resource use objectives\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0e937936",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 6.2 Extreme Point Identification\n",
    "\n",
    "Determine boundary solutions for Pareto front generation:\n",
    "1. **Climate-optimal solution**: Minimize climate change (resource use unconstrained)\n",
    "2. **Resource-optimal solution**: Minimize resource use (climate change unconstrained)\n",
    "\n",
    "These extreme points define the feasible range for epsilon constraints."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 28,
   "id": "b35e4a90",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Creating Instance\n",
      "Instance created\n",
      "optimal solution found:  1.760427258456396\n",
      "Optimization problem solved using Highspy\n",
      "Climate-optimal solution:\n",
      "  Climate change: 1.7604\n",
      "  Resource use: 0.0017\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# 1. Find climate-optimal solution (minimize climate change)\n",
    "methods_climate = {\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'climate change')\": 1,\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'resources')\": 0\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "pulpo_worker_climate = pulpo.PulpoOptimizer(project, database, methods_climate)\n",
    "pulpo_worker_climate.get_lci_data()\n",
    "\n",
    "# Use unconstrained choices for extreme points\n",
    "choices_unconstrained = {\n",
    "    \"Electricity\": {electricity_processes[0]: float('inf'), electricity_processes[1]: float('inf')},\n",
    "    \"Hydrogen\": {hydrogen_processes[0]: float('inf'), hydrogen_processes[1]: float('inf')},\n",
    "    \"Oxygen\": {oxygen_processes[0]: float('inf'), oxygen_processes[1]: float('inf')},\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "pulpo_worker_climate.instantiate(choices=choices_unconstrained, demand=demand, lower_limit=lower_bound)\n",
    "results_climate = pulpo_worker_climate.solve()\n",
    "\n",
    "# Extract optimal impacts\n",
    "climate_optimal_cc = pulpo_worker_climate.instance.impacts_calculated[\"('my project', 'climate change')\"].value\n",
    "climate_optimal_res = pulpo_worker_climate.instance.impacts_calculated[\"('my project', 'resources')\"].value\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Climate-optimal solution:\")\n",

    "# Extract both climate change and resource impacts from Monte Carlo results\n",
    "\n",
    "climate_key = \"('my project', 'climate change')\"\n",
    "resource_key = \"('my project', 'resources')\"\n",
    "\n",
    "if isinstance(mc_results, dict) and len(mc_results) > 0:\n",
    "    print(f\"Extracting both climate change and resource impacts from {len(mc_results)} Monte Carlo iterations...\")\n",
    "    \n",
    "    climate_impacts = []\n",
    "    resource_impacts = []\n",
    "    successful_iterations = 0\n",
    "    \n",
    "    for i, iteration_result in mc_results.items():\n",
    "        try:\n",
    "            if \"error\" in iteration_result:\n",
    "                continue\n",
    "            # Access impact values from the Impacts DataFrame\n",
    "            impacts_df = iteration_result[\"Impacts\"]\n",
    "            climate_value = impacts_df.loc[climate_key, \"Value\"]\n",
    "            resource_value = impacts_df.loc[resource_key, \"Value\"]\n",
    "            \n",
    "            if climate_value is not None and resource_value is not None:\n",
    "                climate_impacts.append(climate_value)\n",
    "                resource_impacts.append(resource_value)\n",
    "                successful_iterations += 1\n",
    "        except (KeyError, AttributeError) as e:\n",
    "            print(f\"Warning: Could not extract impacts from iteration {i}: {e}\")\n",
    "            continue\n",
    "    \n",
    "    print(f\"Successfully extracted impacts from {successful_iterations}/{len(mc_results)} iterations\")\n",

    "        resource_impacts = np.array(resource_impacts)\n",
    "        \n",

    "        climate_mean = np.mean(climate_impacts)\n",

    "        climate_std, resource_std = np.std(climate_impacts, ddof=1), np.std(resource_impacts, ddof=1)\n",

    "        resource_90 = np.percentile(resource_impacts, [5, 95])\n",
    "        correlation = np.corrcoef(climate_impacts, resource_impacts)[0, 1]\n",
    "        print(f\"Climate change: mean {climate_mean:.4f}, std {climate_std:.4f}, \"\n",
    "              f\"90% interval [{climate_90[0]:.4f}, {climate_90[1]:.4f}]\")\n",
    "        print(f\"Resource use:   mean {resource_mean:.4f}, std {resource_std:.4f}, \"\n",
    "              f\"90% interval [{resource_90[0]:.4f}, {resource_90[1]:.4f}]\")\n",
    "        print(f\"Correlation between the two impacts: {correlation:.2f}\")"
   ]

   "source": [
    "## 8. Infeasible Problems\n",
    "\n",
    "Limits that cannot all be met make the optimization problem infeasible. PULPO then raises a `SolveError` (from `pulpo.utils.optimizer`) and loads nothing: the worker keeps its previous solution. The same happens when a solve stops early, for example at a time limit.\n",
    "\n",
    "Limits belong on the processes, flows and impacts that really have one (`lower_limit`, `upper_limit`, `upper_elem_limit`, `upper_imp_limit`, ...), as in section 4. Bounds on every activity through `default_limits` have no physical meaning; they raise a `FutureWarning`, and `default_limits` may be deprecated in a near-future release."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "7f2fafe4",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

    "## 9. Dependent Constraints: Technology Coupling\n",
    "\n",
    "Real-world systems often require interdependent technology operation rules. PULPO's dependent constraints enable specification of relationships between different process scaling levels, allowing for operational constraints, market share limitations, or technology coupling requirements.\n",

    "**Use Cases:**\n",
    "- Maximum renewable energy penetration limits\n",
    "- Technology deployment ratios\n",
    "- Supply chain coordination constraints\n",
    "- Market share limitations\n",
    "- Infrastructure coupling requirements"

   "source": [
    "## 10. Supply Specification: Fixing a Process Output\n",
    "\n",
    "All previous examples are *demand-driven*: a functional unit is specified and the system must deliver it. PULPO also supports *supply-driven* analysis. When a process is given **identical lower and upper limits**, its scaling is fixed to exactly that value, and PULPO automatically activates a **slack variable** for the corresponding reference product. The slack relaxes the product balance, so the fixed output does not need to be absorbed by a final demand — the question becomes:\n",
    "\n",
    "> *“What is the optimal system configuration (and what are its impacts) when this process runs at exactly this level?”*\n",
    "\n",
    "**Use Cases:**\n",
    "- Assessing an existing plant operating at a known production level\n",
    "- Impact accounting for a fixed production quota rather than a functional unit\n",
    "- Analyzing systems where the output is determined by upstream availability (e.g., waste treatment capacity) instead of downstream demand"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "43d8803a",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 10.1 Supply-Driven Optimization: Fixed Methanol Output\n",
    "\n",
    "Fix the methanol synthesis process to a scaling of exactly 1 by passing the **same value as lower and upper limit**. No demand is specified — the fixed supply alone drives the system. The technology choices remain open, so the optimizer still selects the impact-minimal electricity, hydrogen, and oxygen sources needed to run the fixed process."
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "## 11. Goal Programming: Average Transgression Level\n",
    "\n",
    "All previous examples minimize a (weighted) sum of impacts. In many policy-oriented settings — e.g. Planetary-Boundary assessments expressed through the EF 3.1 categories — the question is different: each impact category has a **budget that should not be transgressed**, but some transgression may be unavoidable. PULPO supports this as a goal-programming objective: for each category $h$ with a soft limit (goal) $L_h$, the transgression level is $TL_h = \\text{Impact}_h / L_h$, and the optimizer minimizes the **average transgression**\n",
    "\n",
    "$$\\min \\; \\frac{1}{K} \\sum_{h=1}^{K} \\max\\left(0, \\; TL_h - 1\\right)$$\n",
    "\n",
    "Categories within their budget contribute nothing; transgressed categories contribute proportionally to how far they exceed it. Unlike the hard `upper_imp_limit` constraints from Section 4, goals **can** be exceeded — the problem stays feasible and the solution reports *how much* each budget is blown.\n",
    "\n",
    "### 11.1 An (Invented) Regulatory Budget Scenario\n",
    "\n",
    "Suppose a regulator allocates the methanol producer a per-kg budget in all three impact categories (the numbers are made up for demonstration):\n",
    "\n",
    "| Category | Budget $L_h$ | Attainable minimum |\n",
    "|---|---|---|\n",
    "| climate change | 2.0 | 1.747 (climate-optimal solution) |\n",
    "| air quality | 0.05 | 0.0 |\n",
    "| resources | 0.001 | 0.00057 (resource-optimal solution) |\n",
    "\n",
    "The budgets are deliberately **conflicting**: the climate-optimal technology mix (wind + electrolysis) overshoots the resource budget by 71%, while the resource-optimal mix (gas + SMR) overshoots the climate budget by 73% and the air-quality budget as well. No corner solution satisfies everything — the goal objective must find the best compromise."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 47,
   "id": "de4eedcd",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",

     "text": [

      "Instance created\n",

   "source": [
    "# Fresh worker with ALL three impact categories (weights are ignored in goal mode)\n",
    "methods_goal = {\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'climate change')\": 1,\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'air quality')\": 1,\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'resources')\": 1,\n",
    "}\n",
    "pulpo_worker_goal = pulpo.PulpoOptimizer(project, database, methods_goal)\n",
    "pulpo_worker_goal.get_lci_data()\n",
    "\n",
    "# The invented per-kg-methanol budgets (soft limits)\n",
    "imp_goals = {\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'climate change')\": 2.0,\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'air quality')\": 0.05,\n",
    "    \"('my project', 'resources')\": 0.001,\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "# Same system as Section 3: 1 kg methanol, free technology choices\n",
    "choices_goal = {\n",
    "    \"Electricity\": {electricity_processes[0]: float('inf'), electricity_processes[1]: float('inf')},\n",
    "    \"Hydrogen\": {hydrogen_processes[0]: float('inf'), hydrogen_processes[1]: float('inf')},\n",
    "    \"Oxygen\": {oxygen_processes[0]: float('inf'), oxygen_processes[1]: float('inf')},\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "pulpo_worker_goal.instantiate(\n",
    "    choices=choices_goal,\n",
    "    demand={methanol_process[0]: 1},\n",
    "    lower_limit={oxygen_byproduct[0]: 0},\n",
    "    imp_goals=imp_goals,\n",
    "    objective='goal',\n",
    ")\n",
    "results_goal = pulpo_worker_goal.solve()\n",
    "print(f\"Average transgression level: {pulpo_worker_goal.instance.OBJ():.4f}\")"
   ]

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e6881123",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The compromise is qualitatively different from every weighted-sum solution seen so far:\n",
    "\n",
    "- **Hydrogen is blended**: the optimizer runs electrolysis *and* SMR side by side — a split that no single-objective run produces — because fully committing to either technology would blow one of the budgets much further.\n",
    "- **Air quality sits exactly at its budget** ($TL = 1.0$, transgression 0): the SMR share is expanded precisely up to the point where the air-quality budget becomes binding at the kink of $\\max(0, TL-1)$.\n",
    "- **Climate change and resources are both mildly transgressed** (≈ 19% and ≈ 28%) instead of one of them being blown by > 70%: the average transgression drops to ≈ 0.159, compared to ≈ 0.237 if the climate-optimal mix from Section 3 were assessed against the same budgets.\n",
    "\n",
    "Tightening or relaxing individual budgets shifts this balance — e.g. lowering the resource budget pushes the mix back towards SMR until the climate budget takes over as the binding concern.\n",
    "\n",
    "### 11.3 Yearly Budgets in the Time-Indexed Model\n",
    "\n",
    "The same objective is available in the time-indexed formulation (`pulpo_time.PulpoOptimizerTime`, see the `elec_time_toy` notebook). There the goals apply to the impacts **aggregated over all timesteps** — the natural fit for e.g. an hourly-resolved dispatch problem (8760 steps) with a *total yearly* budget per category:\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "worker = pulpo_time.PulpoOptimizerTime(project, database, methods)\n",
    "worker.get_lci_data()\n",
    "worker.instantiate(\n",
    "    choices=choices, demand=demand,\n",
    "    time_steps=list(range(8760)),                    # hourly resolution\n",
    "    imp_goals={gwp_method: yearly_co2_budget},        # budget on sum over all hours\n",
    "    objective='goal',\n",
    ")\n",
    "worker.solve()\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "The transgression of each category is then evaluated on $\\sum_t \\text{Impact}_{t,h}$, i.e. the optimizer is free to exceed the *hourly-average* budget in some hours as long as the yearly total works out."
   ]
  }
 ],
